name: AI UGC talking-head (avatar) — and its realism stack
type: paid (testing angles fast); organic only with disclosure

shots.visual: Avatar holding the product up close to a phone camera in a real-looking room (bathroom mirror, car, kitchen)
shots.audio_text: Hook from a real review: "okay I need to talk about this necklace because I literally sleep in it"

shots.visual: Medium selfie, natural hand movement, slight handheld wobble
shots.audio_text: Problem in her words: "every gold necklace I owned turned green or snapped"

shots.visual: Cutaways: REAL product B-roll (shower, sea, close-up of clasp)
shots.audio_text: Proof beats: "I showered, I swam, it looks the same"

shots.visual: Back to avatar, smiling, touching the piece
shots.audio_text: Offer + CTA: "they do any 7 for $85, link's below"

prompts.prompt: Choose a 25-40 female avatar filmed in a bathroom or car, natural lighting, casual clothes. Script: [paste]. Settings: "casual" tone, add 2-3 natural pauses, slight pitch variation, 9:16.
Add background room tone, a 3-5% handheld shake, auto-captions in TikTok style, cut every 2-4s, cover the mouth area with B-roll at least 40% of the time.

paid_ads.title: Khazanay Pakistan: Clinic presenter in scrubs (orthopedic shoes)
paid_ads.what: A woman in navy scrubs in a clinic corridor: "Let me tell you that you don't need a new body. You just need better support… it's not always an injury… unsupported shoes… plantar fasciitis". 70 s, run as 2 near-identical ads.
paid_ads.how: A specialist look-alike (scrubs, not a named doctor), a reframe sentence first, then cause, then product category. Captions mid-frame.

paid_ads.title: Blossom Essentials Skin: Short AI-UGC "only balm I'll ever buy" (Blossom Essentials, 3 variants)
paid_ads.what: Three 24-33 s UGC cuts: "This is the only skin balm I will ever spend money on… I've tried everything, from prescription to specialist." Different women, same script skeleton.
paid_ads.how: Write one 60-word script and record it with 3-10 faces (AI UGC or creators). Change only the opener.

qa_checklist: Hook lands in the first 1.5 s (video) or is readable at thumbnail size (static / slide 1).
Removal test: delete the product from the script. If it still makes sense, rewrite so the product is the payoff.
Matches the reference structure (same beat order and length band) before any creative twist.
Uses only real product imagery for the product; AI is for backgrounds, characters or b-roll, and is disclosed where required.
Every claim is on the brand's approved-claims list (PDP); no invented stats, reviews, doctors or customers.
Captions burned in and inside the safe zone; sound-off still understandable.
One clear CTA that matches the landing page offer.
Three hook variants delivered for the same body (test hooks, not whole new ads).
Avoid: Avatars reading a script word-perfect look fake; add fillers ("like", "honestly") and a stumble.
Avoid: Avatars may not claim a personal experience they did not have in places where that is regulated; label AI and keep claims to product facts.
Avoid: Never show the avatar "wearing" AI jewelry; cut to real product footage.
Avoid: Ranked by researchers: avatar reading a script = F tier; avatar inside a story or skit performs better.
inputs: BRAND (name, product, price, offer, audience, proof points, banned claims)
ASSETS (real product photos/video, logo, fonts, colors)
outputs: brands/<brand-slug>.md with 3 concepts in the output schema below
per concept: script/slide copy, shot list, on-screen text, caption, CTA, 3 hook variants, prompts used
